reader: source-only reader (publisher pictures + page facts); no analyzer, solver or model output was run or seen
frontHow: The entrance door into the wiatrolap opens onto the covered porch along the bottom edge of the ground-plan picture, and the site-plan picture puts its entry arrow at the bottom; the front elevation (przod) shows that door between two small windows.

overall.includes: Printed on the site-plan picture (rzut dzialki), not on the floor plan, which carries no dimensions. Both figures bound the dashed wall outline: the depth runs from the rear living-room bay to the front wall of the right-hand bedroom block. The roof overhang, the front porch and the rear terraces lie outside the wall outline but inside the same bounding box corners.

outlineNote: Two blocks side by side and offset front-to-back (left block with kitchen and living room sits further back, right bedroom block further forward), plus a shallow living-room bay stepping out of the rear wall; a porch fills the front-left recess and a covered terrace the rear-right recess, all under one roof.

bodies.name: main
bodies.position: the whole house; one roof covers both offset blocks, the front porch and the rear-right terrace

bodies.name: rear bay
bodies.position: rectangular living-room projection on the rear wall, roughly the middle third of the width (left of centre seen from the front), with its own small cross gable

uncertain: The floor plan has no printed dimensions; overall size comes only from the site-plan picture (1072 x 1012 between plot offsets of 400).
The section prints 681 from terrain (-0,45) to ridge (+6,36); the page text gives 6.8 m.

The two side elevations are both captioned 'elewacja boczna'; assigned from the plan: two bedroom windows plus a recessed terrace door = RIGHT, two small windows (pantry, kitchen) plus a recessed porch window = LEFT.

LEFT count of 3 includes the utility-room (pom. gosp.) window that faces left inside the front porch recess; RIGHT count of 3 includes the living-room door that faces right inside the rear terrace recess. Without those recessed openings the gable walls have 2 each.
The rear gable over the living-room bay is the roof of a ground-level projection in a single-storey house; it is listed as a body, not as a dormer.
